claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you asking about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son, **Alex**.

Let me start by gathering some details about Alex. **How old is Alex, and what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old. His birthday is in March 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So Alex was born in March 2016, making him 8 years old.

**Is Alex living with you in the UK at the moment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Alex is living with you in Manchester.

**Are you responsible for maintaining Alex, and is he your child or are you a guardian/carer for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's my son and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training (such as an apprenticeship), or is he not in education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8, so he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course, thank you for confirming that. Alex is in primary school, which means he's in full-time education.

**Are you currently receiving any benefits such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**What is your current employment status? Are you working, self-employed, unemployed, or something else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know you're working full-time.

**What is your approximate annual household income (before tax)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd say it's around £45,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have a different residency status in the UK (such as settled status, visa, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just to complete my assessment, **has Alex ever lived outside the UK, or has he always lived in the UK since birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's always lived here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation:
- Alex is your 8-year-old son, born in March 2016
- He lives with you in Manchester, UK
- He's in full-time education (primary school)
- You are responsible for maintaining him
- You are a British citizen
- Alex has always lived in the UK
- You are working full-time with an annual household income of approximately £45,000
- You are not currently receiving Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility criteria, I can now provide you with my outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

To summarize: Alex meets all the eligibility requirements. He's under 16, in full-time education, living with you in the UK as your dependent child, and you're a British citizen. Your income doesn't prevent you from claiming Child Benefit.

If you haven't already, you can proceed with making a claim through the official UK government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?
